Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 7:46 P.M.

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Martinez, Chief of Police Bertelsen, Director of Administrative

Community Development Marquez, Director of Information Technology and Library Services Graf, Director of Public
Works/City Engineer Delgadillo, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia, and Chief Deputy City Clerk Garcia.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

The City Council reconvened at 7:46 P.M.; City Attorney Martinez announced the following regarding Closed Session:
The Council heard Items 1, 2, and 3, and the Council will reconvene at the end of the regular meeting to hear Items 4, 5,
and 6. Item 1 – The City Council heard a presentation from its negotiating team regarding price and terms regarding a
potential lease or purchase of property, no reportable action; Item 2 – City Council heard a presentation from its
negotiating team concerning price and terms of a potential lease and the Council provided direction, no further reportable
action; and Item 3 – Pursuant to the Azusa personnel rules, the City Council reviewed an employee discipline matter and
by a vote of 4-1, voted to sustain the discipline imposed by the department head in accordance with the City’s personnel
rules.

CEREMONIAL

1. Presentation of Proclamation proclaiming the month of June 2021 as LGBTA+ Pride Month in the City of Azusa

  Moved by Mayor Pro-Tem Avila, seconded by Councilmember Alvarez and carried by unanimous vote of the Council
  to proclaim the month of June 2021 as LGBTQ+ Pride Month in the City of Azusa:

  AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ
  NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
  ABSTAIN:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

PUBLIC COMMENT

Arturo Ortega, Azusa Unified School District Superintendent, provided highlights and updates about the School District.

Ryan Serrano, Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors Representative, provided updates regarding the safe reopening
of Los Angeles County; provided information regarding vaccinations; and provided information about available resources.

REPORTS, UPDATES AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez provided a COVID-19 update stating City Hall is now completely open; Staff is continuing to
work on increasing vaccinations in the City; and Staff is working on an educational workshop in conjunction with Los
Angeles County Department of Health, a local medical provider, and a parent advocate, to provide information to those
individuals that are reluctant to get a vaccine.

Council Comments

Mayor Pro-Tem Avila expressed his condolences to the family of Richard Sanchez and requested that the meeting be
adjourned in his honor; thanked the Veteran’s Memorial Day Committee for their Memorial Day Ceremony;
congratulated the St. Francis of Rome promotion class; congratulated the Lady Aztecs Softball Team on an undefeated
season and wished them luck in CIF; congratulated all of the high school graduates; commended and thanked the Azusa
Police Department for their hard work on an incident that took place over the weekend; thanked Superintendent Ortega for
his announcements; and, on behalf of the family of Mr. George Romero, thanked everyone for their well wishes.

Councilmember Macias congratulated all of the graduates in the City of Azusa; inquired about the swim lessons start date;
requested an update on the clock at CVS; and inquired about the process for speed bump installation in residential
neighborhoods.
PAGE TWO – 6/7/2021
 Councilmember Alvarez provided information regarding the Foothill Transit meeting that he recently attended; and
requested that street lanes be repainted on westbound First Street and Azusa Avenue, eastbound Foothill Boulevard and
Azusa Avenue, westbound on Foothill Boulevard and San Gabriel Avenue.

Director of Community Resources Carpenter provided an update on the swimming pool and vaccine clinics.

Councilmember Mendez congratulated Gladstone High School Counselor Abdo on his retirement; congratulated the
graduating class of 2021; commended the officers for their work during the incident on Foothill Boulevard; inquired about
an incident which took place in the riverbed; requested an update on the homeless situation in the riverbed; inquired about
the homeless count and enforcement jurisdiction; requested a formal update from the Homelessness Ad-hoc Committee to
be placed on the agenda for the following Council Meeting; and inquired about Gold Line TAP Card readers in the City of
Azusa.

Chief of Police Bertelsen provided information regarding an assault that took place in the riverbed; provided information
regarding the homeless in the riverbed and locations in which enforcement can be taken by Azusa Police Department; and
discussed patrol operations surrounding the Gold Line and homeless outreach on the train.

City Manager Gonzalez provided further information regarding the homeless count, enforcement in the riverbed, and
Lario Park.

Mayor Gonzales provided information regarding the Homeless Ad-hoc Committee meeting that he attended with
Councilmember Alvarez; requested that a discussion regarding the homeless issues in the riverbed be placed on agenda
for the next City Council meeting; discussed the homeless situation at Lario Park; thanked the Veteran’s Committee for
the Memorial Day Ceremony; requested certificates for the Christbridge Academy graduates; announced the LeRoy
Harris Kelly III Annual Walk on June 12, 2021 at Veteran’s Freedom Park; and announced a candlelight vigil in memory
of the individuals that lost their lives to COVID-19 on June 26, 2021.

Chief of Police Bertelsen stated the requirements for requesting that a homeless individual leave a specific area.

SCHEDULED ITEMS – CITY COUNCIL

AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING
SECTION 30-137 (C) OF THE AZUSA MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO ADMINISTRATIVE CITATIONS AND
FINES FOR VIOLATIONS OF THE CITY OF AZUSA’S FIREWORKS REGULATIONS

City Attorney Martinez presented the Item stating that at the May 3, 2021 City Council Meeting, Staff was directed to
prepare an Urgency Ordinance increasing the fines related to the discharge of illegal fireworks; the fines would be
established at $1,000 for the first violation, $2,000 for the second violation, and $5,000 for the third violation occurring
within five years; a provision was included to state that any violations after the five year period, the fine would continue
to be $5,000; and the Urgency Ordinance would take effect immediately after adoption.

In response to questions posed by the Council, Chief of Police Bertelsen stated that approximately two-thirds of the
citations issued were to Azusa residents.

Councilmember Mendez offered Urgency Ordinance No. 2021-03 entitled:

AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AZUSA, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING
SECTION 30-137(c) OF THE AZUSA MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO ADMINISTRATIVE CITATIONS AND
FINES FOR VIOLATIONS OF THE CITY OF AZUSA’S FIREWORKS REGULATIONS

Moved by Councilmember Mendez, seconded by Mayor Pro-Tem Avila, and carried by unanimous vote of the Council to
introduce and adopt Urgency Ordinance No. 2021-03 amending Section 30-137(c) of the Azusa Municipal Code related to
administrative citations and fines for violations of the City of Azusa’s fireworks regulations.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, MACIAS, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ
